discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution and entanglement-based secure communication

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur K. Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the fundamental principles of quantum mechanics, namely the no-cloning property and the disturbance caused by measurement, can guarantee the secrecy of communication. Ekert (1991) independently linked key distribution to entanglement, making security testable through violation of Bell's inequality. This turned the most puzzling features of quantum theory into a practical resource. Their ideas founded the field of quantum information science. They led directly to quantum teleportation (Bennett, Brassard and co-workers, 1993) and to device-independent security, and they inspired a generation of experiments: fibre networks, free-space links and satellite quantum communication over more than a thousand kilometres. Quantum key distribution is now deployed commercially and is at the centre of a global effort toward a quantum internet. Few conceptual discoveries in physics have gone so directly from foundations to technology.
